title: Nuclear Engineering, B.S. (College of Engineering)
notes: Post-2024-25 curriculum-overhaul year, built from the archived 2024-25 bulletin's Suggested Academic Plan and Program Requirements tabs, fetched directly. This is the FIRST catalog year with the current NUCE 321/NUCE 322 in-house thermal-fluids sequence (Introduction to Thermal-Fluid Sciences for Nuclear Engineers I/II) replacing the older ME 300/ME 320/ME 410 support courses (compare NUCE-2022.json/NUCE-2023.json), NUCE 420 (Radiological Safety) promoted from a Nuclear Engineering elective option to a required core course, and NUCE 297 existing as this program's own named First-Year Seminar course for the first time. Suggested Academic Plan is byte-identical to the 2025-26 edition (NUCE-2025.json) and functionally unchanged in the current 2026-27 live bulletin that NUCE-2026.json itself is built from -- same course sequence, same per-semester credit totals, same 129-credit program total. This year's own archived Program Requirements elective list reads BME 406, NUCE 405/408/409/428/470/490/496/497, or 500-level NUCE courses with adviser approval (420 already excluded here since it's required core this year) -- the same real underlying department elective rule NUCE-2026.json's own 'Nuclear Engineering elective' match already encodes (400-level NUCE except 401, required core, and independent-study/special-topics codes), so that slot is reproduced identically from NUCE-2026.json rather than re-derived, since the rule is a year-independent department policy, not a 2026-specific one. Same real CHEM 110 -> MATH 22 -> MATH 21 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 3 prerequisite-chain gap and the same EMCH 315/EMCH 316 same-term scheduling conflict (EMCH 316 needs EMCH 315 as a strict prior-term prerequisite) exist in this year's own bulletin Suggested Academic Plan too -- both fixed the identical way NUCE-2026.json fixes them (MATH 3/4/21/22 added across Semesters 1-4; EMCH 316 moved to the following term with both Nuclear Engineering elective slots consolidated into the final semester). max_credits_per_semester raised to 19, same as NUCE-2026.json, for the same reason.
